node_greeting.speaker: Abenthy
node_greeting.text: You want to learn the ways of a trouper, do you? The road teaches as much as any master, but only if you ask the right questions. How do you approach a stranger's secret?

choices.text: I ask plainly. Curiosity is the only honest key.
I watch and wait. A secret offered is safer than a secret taken.

text_by_flag.text: Honest, if a little loud. Curiosity opens doors, but it also leaves fingerprints. Remember: a trouper listens twice for every word spoken.
Wise. Patience is a kind of power, and power should be quiet. A trouper learns to read the silence between the words.

node_lesson.speaker: Abenthy
node_lesson.text: Here is your first lesson, then. Every story has three threads: what is said, what is meant, and what is feared. Hold all three at once, and you hold the audience.

node_practice.speaker: Abenthy
node_practice.text: Now, practice. I tell a tale of a farmer who sold his shadow. Do you ask after the buyer, or do you ask after the price?

choices.text: Who would buy a shadow? The buyer is the mystery.
What did the farmer gain? The price tells the worth.

node_encouragement.speaker: Abenthy
node_encouragement.text: You reach for the stranger first. That is the heart of it. Keep that hunger, and you will learn faster than most.

node_caution.speaker: Abenthy
node_caution.text: You weigh the cost before the tale. There is wisdom in that, too. Not every audience wants to be startled.
